edits.old: The request and response fields of the interaction write, the Idempotency-Key rule, the failure mapping and the compensation mechanism are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0375; ASM-0538), so the suite asserts the outcomes named in section 7 and not a wire shape it would have to invent.
edits.new: The interaction write follows the contract RWB-P1-E1066-CON (GAP-0375, GAP-0504, GAP-0505; ASM-0538). The append path is `/cases/{caseId}/interactions` on the rwb-source-data base, called under the `rwb_source_data` login (DP-02), with `InteractionRequest` in, `Interaction` out, property names from the API specification and a required `Idempotency-Key` header. P1 writes the entry, its local decision record and its outbox row in one transaction in `rwb_source_data` and answers 201 with the entry identifier and caseSeq. A repeat with the same key and body returns the stored entry with the same caseSeq and writes no second row; the same key with a different body answers 409; a missing key answers 400 with MSG-GEN-004. A missing required value answers 422 with MSG-GEN-001, a missing Case record C right 403 with MSG-P4-002, an unknown or out-of-scope case 404 with MSG-P4-003, and a failed write 503 with MSG-P1-022. The required flags of the ledger values are those of the contract, settled at its baseline review. The caller treats any non-2xx answer as a failed action and never keeps an action without its entry. rwb-case records each case action in its link table `interaction_link` (RWB-P3-E1066-APP): `PENDING` before the append, `COMMITTED` after 201, and `REFUSED` when the action is not applied.
